# Petra Demo & Judge Defense

This document is for presenting Petra without overclaiming it.

## One-sentence pitch

**Petra is a browser-based Petri-dish sandbox where evolution is generated by a reproducible spatial stochastic model, and every major biological rule can be traced back to its source and assumptions.**

## Why it is not “just an animation”

The animation is downstream of:
- nutrient diffusion;
- resource-limited population growth;
- concentration-dependent drug response;
- stochastic reproduction-linked mutations;
- genotype-specific resistance/fitness;
- spatial competition;
- seeded stochasticity.

If the renderer is replaced with plain heatmaps, the same biological trajectory still exists.

## Why it is not “just an LLM wrapper”

The flagship does not need an LLM at all.

An LLM may later explain an event log using Petra's source library, but:
- it does not choose mutations;
- it does not invent MIC values;
- it does not decide survival;
- it does not calculate authoritative biology.

## Strong 90-second demonstration

### 0–10 s — establish the world
Open the flagship *E. coli / ciprofloxacin* scenario.

Show:
- live dish;
- nutrient overlay;
- population;
- seed;
- scenario provenance badge.

Say:
“Everything in the dish is being generated from the same reproducible simulation state—this isn't a video.”

### 10–25 s — let the colony grow
Run accelerated time.

Show nutrient depletion and spatial expansion.

Open a local inspector briefly:
- local resource;
- local growth;
- lineage.

### 25–50 s — apply pressure
Paint or place a ciprofloxacin band/gradient.

Sensitive areas stall or decline according to the concentration-response curve.

Say:
“The drug doesn't tell the cells which mutation to make. Mutations happen on reproduction; the environment changes which lineages succeed.”

### 50–70 s — lineage event
When a resistant lineage becomes important:
- event marker;
- focus camera;
- lineage tree;
- genotype;
- MIC;
- relative fitness;
- source card.

If the chosen demo seed has a pre-existing low-frequency lineage before dosing, point it out.

### 70–85 s — reproducibility
Replay the same seed/interventions.

Then change seed or fork the run.

Say:
“The same seed reproduces the same stochastic history; changing the seed gives a genuinely different evolutionary trajectory.”

### 85–90 s — scientific honesty
Open Sources/Assumptions.

Say:
“We also expose where we combine studies or use approximations rather than pretending this is a digital twin.”

## Three-minute demonstration extension

Add:
- no-drug fork vs ciprofloxacin fork;
- compare genotype frequencies;
- show a fitness trade-off after removing pressure;
- show spatial front access changing which lineage expands.

If phage is implemented and verified, it can be an optional second scenario—not a rushed distraction from the flagship.

## Expected judge questions

### “How realistic is this?”
Answer:
Petra is a mechanistic educational model rather than a full-cell or clinical digital twin. It models the mechanisms needed for the experiment at population/spatial scale and labels transferred/calibrated assumptions explicitly.

### “Are you simulating every bacterium?”
No. That would be computationally wasteful and would imply precision we do not have. Petra uses local lineage cohorts and continuous fields, then renders representative bacteria/colony texture.

### “How are mutations generated?”
From reproduction events. Rare mutation counts are sampled probabilistically from divisions, using bounded stochastic methods. Antibiotics alter selection, not a “mutation button.”

### “Where do resistance numbers come from?”
For the flagship, curated MIC/relative-fitness states come from Marcusson et al. 2009; mutation-supply evidence comes from Huseby et al. 2017; the concentration-response shape comes from Regoes et al. 2004. The interface shows that those studies are composed rather than pretending they were one experiment.

### “What is AI doing?”
The canonical simulator is mechanistic. A future trained surrogate can accelerate repeated runs and be compared against the mechanistic engine. An LLM can explain events with sources. AI does not replace biological authority.

### “Why not use a neural network to predict evolution?”
Because the important scientific story is causal and inspectable. A model trained on Petra is only useful if its error is measurable against the simulator and it remains inside a known training domain.

### “Is this useful beyond school?”
Potentially as an interactive teaching/research-exploration interface and as a framework for comparing mechanistic scenarios. It should not be presented as a medical treatment planner.

### “Can it predict which mutation will happen?”
It produces probabilistic trajectories under a curated genotype graph and parameter set. It does not predict the complete genomic evolution of a real culture.

### “Why does the most resistant strain not always win?”
Fitness is multidimensional: growth cost, spatial access, resource competition, timing, and stochastic founder effects can matter. Spatial experiments such as Baym et al. demonstrate that access to the advancing front can constrain outcomes.

## Things to avoid saying

Do not say:
- “This perfectly simulates real bacteria.”
- “This predicts antibiotic treatment.”
- “Every dot is a bacterium.”
- “The AI knows how the bacteria evolve.”
- “The antibiotic makes them mutate.”
- “These exact parameters all come from the same experiment.”

Prefer:
- “mechanistic educational simulator”;
- “literature-backed component model”;
- “transferred approximation”;
- “representative visual”;
- “stochastic trajectory”;
- “same seed is reproducible.”

## Demo reliability without cheating

It is legitimate to:
- save and select a seed that produces a clear educational trajectory;
- preload a named scenario;
- accelerate simulation time;
- use event-focused camera transitions.

It is **not** legitimate to:
- special-case that seed;
- spawn a resistant lineage because a demo timer reached 30 seconds;
- make renderer particles cause mutations;
- silently use different rules in demo mode.

## Offline readiness

The core demo should run from local/static assets:
- no LLM required;
- no remote model required;
- citations can be bundled;
- no network request required for simulation.

This is both technically safer and a stronger answer to judges.
